verdicts.trueWording: very much described in terms of components that can be interacted with
verdicts.note: Body para on the Keep: quote verbatim; continues 'with the wider existential, political or metaphysical implications left to the GM to interpret.' Raw HTML fetched (200).

verdicts.trueWording: feels like a living, breathing place, complete with a church, merchant caravans, guilds, a tavern
verdicts.note: Same paragraph; quote verbatim, and the living-place framing is the page's own ('But it also feels like a living, breathing place'). List continues 'a money-lender... prices for drinks listed etc.'

verdicts.trueWording: But the NPCs have motivations and character traits
verdicts.note: Verbatim, inside the comment signed 'PrinceofNothing says: January 27, 2019 at 10:50 am', in his bracketed rebuttal under '[Mike Mearls review]' to summarised point '1. NPCs don't have names in Keep therefore the module is bad.' Author and comment-section location both confirmed.

verdicts.trueWording: 359 pages of detailed information about keyed locations in the city
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the content walkthrough. Page adds 'and on other maps in the Ptolus "package"' - a widening the claim does not contradict. Author countzeroasl, Storytelling and Gaming, confirmed on page.

verdicts.trueWording: It covers what it looks like as an everyday resident
verdicts.note: Verbatim. Sentence before: 'The next section is a deep dive into the "feel" of Ptolus and what it is like to live there.'

verdicts.trueWording: the urbancrawl key doesn't represent all the information that you might prep about the city
verdicts.note: Verbatim, first sentence under the 'THE KEY' heading of 'Thinking About Urbancrawls - Part 4: Experimental City Hexes' (Jan 14, 2015); site author Justin Alexander confirmed on page.

verdicts.trueWording: Rooms are described in detail for the DM. Detail that is meaningless and has no impact on the game
verdicts.note: Verbatim; the no-impact limb is the immediately following sentence. Post 'Curse of Strahd', posted March 14, 2016 by Bryce Lynch.

verdicts.trueWording: Three sentences are used when one will do
verdicts.note: Verbatim, same paragraph; followed by 'Six are used when it needed two, or three.'

verdicts.trueWording: The entries are so long that the important bits are lost
verdicts.note: Verbatim, same paragraph, immediately after the Wall of Text sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: Here's a masterpiece of creative read-aloud writing!!! "You find something on the ground."
verdicts.note: Verbatim inside the read-aloud paragraph, quoted from the adventure among other read-aloud examples; Bryce notes these are for a wandering-monster table.

verdicts.trueWording: The most valuable part... is the detailed gazetteer describing the neighborhoods and prominent locations
verdicts.note: Verbatim; article title confirms the subject is 'D&D 5e's 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide'.

verdicts.trueWording: The location descriptions are full of flavorful NPCs, background hooks
verdicts.note: Verbatim, next sentence after the gazetteer line; continues 'to draw players into the fabric of the city, and concrete reasons to visit each location.'

verdicts.trueWording: The calendar is detailed with fictional names for the months and the days of the week, plus festival events
verdicts.note: Verbatim, in the cultures-and-world section; covers month names, weekday names and festivals.

verdicts.trueWording: From premise... to core material and a gazetteer, it serves two purposes
verdicts.note: Verbatim, in the article body above the 'Beth Rimmels' author bio; thread starter/byline 'brimmels' = Beth Rimmels, confirmed on page.

verdicts.trueWording: in the 2014 book, Chapter One was about creating your own world
verdicts.note: Verbatim, in the '2014 vs. 2024' section of the body; continues 'and includes a section on creating your own campaign.'
